# Types

The records, enums, aliases and opaque types of the builtin schema. The language's own types (`int`, `float`, `bool`, `text`, `color`, `length`, `duration`, `T?`, `[T]`, `Async<T>` and the rest) are in spec.md, section 7.1.

## Records

### `AccessPoint`

A Wi-Fi network in range, from NetworkManager's last scan; access
points of one network name are one entry (the strongest). Keyed by
`ssid`.

Keyed by `ssid`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ssid` | `text` | The network's name. |
| `strength` | `float` | Signal strength, 0 to 1. |
| `secure` | `bool` | It needs a password: a WPA, WPA2 or WPA3 personal or a WEP network, which `connect_with` joins (a network menu's password field). An open or Enhanced Open network takes none, and an enterprise (802.1X) one joins through its saved profile, with `connect()`. |
| `active` | `bool` | It is the network joined. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action connect()` | Joins it: with its saved connection if there is one, else a new one (for a `secure` network NetworkManager asks its secret agent for the password); an enterprise (802.1X) network with no saved profile is refused (it is set up in the system's network settings). A failure, including one NetworkManager reports later (no password, a wrong one, a timeout), is `network.failed`. |
| `action connect_with(password: text)` | Joins a `secure` network with `password` (its WPA key or WEP key), saved in its connection: a network menu's password field. On any other network it fails. A failure is `network.failed`. |

### `App`

An installed app, from its desktop entry (watched live).

Keyed by `id`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `text` | Its desktop entry id (`org.gnome.Nautilus`, `kde-dolphin`: the entry's path below `applications/`, `/` as `-`, without `.desktop`). |
| `name` | `text` | Its name, in the user's language. |
| `comment` | `text?` | Its comment, if the entry has one. |
| `icon` | `text` | Its icon: `image h.app.icon`. An icon name of the desktop's icon theme, or a path; `application-x-executable` when the entry names none the theme has. |
| `categories` | `[text]` | Its desktop entry categories. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action launch()` | Starts it (its `Exec` line, detached; in a terminal when the entry asks for one) and counts the launch for frecency: `on activate { h.app.launch() }`. |

### `AudioDevice`

An audio sink or source, from PipeWire.

Keyed by `id`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `int` | Its PipeWire id. |
| `name` | `text` | Its node name. |
| `description` | `text` | A readable description of it. |
| `volume` | `float rw` | Volume, 0 to 1, on the cubic scale `wpctl` and `pactl` show (above 1 when another program amplified it). Writable: `audio.sink.volume -= dy * 0.05`; every channel takes the new value. |
| `muted` | `bool rw` | Muted. Writable: `audio.sink.muted = !audio.sink.muted`. |
| `icon` | `text` | An icon name for its volume and mute state. |
| `default` | `bool` | It is the default device. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action make_default()` | Makes it the default device. |

### `BluetoothDevice`

### `Canvas`

What `canvas { draw: (c) => … }` draws on, with the paint API the
renderer uses.

A live handle, not data: it compares, but `persist` and settings files cannot store it.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | `float` | The canvas width. |
| `height` | `float` | The canvas height. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `fn fill(paint: paint)` | Fills with `paint`. |
| `fn stroke(paint: paint, width: length = 1)` | Strokes with `paint`, `width` wide. |
| `fn line(x1: float, y1: float, x2: float, y2: float)` | A line from (`x1`, `y1`) to (`x2`, `y2`). |
| `fn rect(x: float, y: float, w: float, h: float)` | A rectangle at (`x`, `y`), `w` wide and `h` high. |
| `fn circle(x: float, y: float, r: float)` | A circle centred at (`x`, `y`) with radius `r`. |
| `fn text(t: text, x: float, y: float)` | Text `t` at (`x`, `y`). |

### `Date`

A date and time of day, such as `clock.today`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `year` | `int` | The year. |
| `month` | `int` | The month, 1 to 12. |
| `day` | `int` | The day of the month, 1 to 31. |
| `weekday` | `int` | The day of the week. |
| `hour` | `int?` | The hour, 0 to 23; null for a date without a time of day (`clock.today`, a calendar's days). `clock.now` and a notification's `time` have one: `n.time.format("%H:%M")`. |
| `minute` | `int?` | The minute, 0 to 59; null when `hour` is. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `fn month_start() -> Date` | The first day of its month: `clock.today.month_start()`. |
| `fn add(days: int = 0, months: int = 0, years: int = 0) -> Date` | Moves by days, months and years, keeping its time of day: `month.add(months: -1)`. |
| `fn format(pattern: text) -> text` | Formats with a strftime pattern: `month.format("%B %Y")`. |

### `Day`

A cell of a month grid, from `calendar.days(month)`.

Keyed by `date`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | `Date` | The day's date. |
| `in_month` | `bool` | It falls in the month asked for; the grid is padded with the days of the months around it. |
| `today` | `bool` | It is today. |
| `weekend` | `bool` | It falls on a weekend. |

### `Drop`

What another program drops on an element (design.md, "Drag and drop"):
files, an app or text, as `on drop(d: Drop, at: int)`. `kind` says
which; the other fields are empty. A drag inside the shell delivers the
`drag:` source's own value instead (`on drop(p: Pin, at: int)`).

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `DropKind` | What was dropped: `files`, `app` or `text`. |
| `files` | `[path]` | The dropped files. |
| `app` | `App?` | The dropped app. |
| `text` | `text` | The dropped text. |

### `Hit`

A launcher search result: the app, its score and the matched ranges.

Keyed by `app.id`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` | `App` | The app found. |
| `score` | `float` | Its score: fuzzy match plus frecency (higher first). |
| `ranges` | `[Range]` | The matched character ranges of its name: `marks: h.ranges`. Empty when the query matched its keywords or generic name instead. |

A key press: `on key(k: Key)`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `text` | The key's name, such as `Escape`, `Return` or `a`. |
| `text` | `text` | The text the key types; empty for keys that type none. |
| `ctrl` | `bool` | Ctrl is held. |

### `Node`

A node of the tree: `self`, or an element given an `id:`.

A live handle, not data: it compares, but `persist` and settings files cannot store it.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hover` | `bool` | The pointer is over it (latched while dragging). |
| `pressed` | `bool` | A pointer button is held down on it. |
| `focused` | `bool` | It has keyboard focus. |
| `selected` | `bool` | It is the selected item of a `list`; arrow keys move the selection. |
| `width` | `float` | Its laid-out width. `when self.width < 300 { … }` is a container query, with 4 px hysteresis so it cannot flicker. |
| `height` | `float` | Its laid-out height. |
| `open` | `bool` | A `popup` (or another surface) is open: from the moment its `open` turns true (or the pointer opens a `trigger: hover` one) until it turns false, as its exit pose starts. False on other elements. `when cal.open { bg: $surface.hi }` styles an anchor while its popup shows. |
| `box` | `Rect` | Its laid-out box, in its surface's logical pixels from the top-left corner of the surface's box (paint offsets, transforms and poses not applied). A popup's own box is where it sits in the surface it opens from; a bar's, panel's or OSD's is at 0, 0. It updates a frame after layout moves it, and springs like any value: `x: item.box.x - row.box.x ~ $motion.spatial`. It may drive anything that does not lay it out again, through any chain of bindings: paint props (`x`, `y`, `opacity`, colours, transforms; a surface's effects), the size of a `place: absolute` element it is not inside, or what is on another surface that reads nothing back; a load error shows the loop otherwise. `width` and `height` of another node are the same fact. |

### `Notification`

A desktop notification, keyed by `id`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `int` | Its identity. |
| `app` | `NotificationApp` | The app that sent it. |
| `summary` | `text` | Its summary line. |
| `body` | `text` | Its body, which may hold basic markup (`markup: basic`). |
| `image` | `text?` | An image it carries, if any: a path. |
| `urgency` | `Urgency` | `low`, `normal` or `critical`. |
| `timeout` | `duration?` | How long the sender asked it to show; null leaves it to the shell: `after n.timeout ?? 6s { n.expire() }`. |
| `persistent` | `bool` | The sender asked it never to expire (an `expire_timeout` of 0): a shell keeps its popup with `after n.timeout ?? 6s while !n.persistent { n.expire() }`. |
| `time` | `Date` | When it arrived. |
| `actions` | `[NotificationAction]` | The buttons it offers. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action expire()` | Ends its popup, as a timeout does; it stays in `all`, still open (its actions still reach the sender) until dismissed. |
| `action dismiss()` | Closes it: `on secondary { n.dismiss() }`. |
| `action activate()` | Invokes its default action: `on click { n.activate() }`. |

### `NotificationAction`

A button a notification offers.

Keyed by `id`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `text` | Its identity: the key the sender gave it. |
| `label` | `text` | Its label: `button a.label`. |
| `notification` | `int` | The notification it belongs to. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action invoke()` | Invokes it: `on click { a.invoke() }`. The sender is told; the notification closes unless it is resident. |

### `Screen`

A monitor. `id` is its identity (make, model and description, with
` #2` for a second identical one): what a `bar` instance is keyed and
pinned by, kept across a replug to another port. `name` is the
connector (`DP-1`).

Keyed by `id`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `text` | Its identity: make, model and description, with ` #2` for a second identical one. Kept across a replug to another port. |
| `name` | `text` | Its connector name, such as `DP-1`. |
| `make` | `text` | Its maker. |
| `model` | `text` | Its model. |
| `description` | `text` | A readable description of it. |
| `scale` | `float` | Its scale factor. |
| `width` | `float` | Its width in logical pixels. |
| `height` | `float` | Its height in logical pixels. |
| `focused` | `bool` | It has keyboard focus. |

### `TrayItem`

An item in the system tray (StatusNotifierItem), keyed by `id`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `text` | Its identity: its bus name and object path. |
| `title` | `text` | Its title. |
| `icon` | `text` | Its icon: `image item.icon`. An icon name, or the path of a picture (an icon the app ships, or pixels it sent). |
| `tooltip` | `text?` | Its tooltip, if it has one. |
| `status` | `text` | `Active`, `Passive` or `NeedsAttention`. |
| `menu` | `TrayMenu` | Its menu. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action activate()` | Its primary action: `on click { item.activate() }`. An item that is only a menu (`ItemIsMenu`: most libappindicator apps) opens its menu instead (`menu.opened`), as the StatusNotifierItem spec asks. The app is told where: the bottom-left corner of the element pressed, in its screen's logical pixels (where an app showing a menu of its own puts it). |
| `action secondary()` | Its secondary action, told where as `activate()` is. |
| `action scroll(dy: float)` | Scrolls on it by `dy` wheel notches (one click is 1, a touchpad sends fractions; positive is down, as `on scroll(dy)` gives it). The app gets 120 per notch, positive up, as KDE's tray sends it. |

### `TrayMenu`

A tray item's menu (DBusMenu).

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` | `text` | The tray item it belongs to. |
| `items` | `[TrayMenuItem]` | Its entries, as the app last laid them out; empty when the item has no menu. |
| `opened` | `bool` | It is open: true from `open()` until `close()` (or the item going away). A popup shows it with `open: item.menu.opened`, and calls `item.menu.close()` when it closes. One flag per item, not per screen: a bar on every screen keeps which screen opened it (`on secondary { item.menu.open(); menu_screen = screen }`, `open: item.menu.opened && menu_screen == screen`). |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action open()` | Opens it: `on secondary { item.menu.open() }`. The app is told it opens (and may update its entries first), and `opened` becomes true; a `popup { open: item.menu.opened … }` drawing `items` is what shows a DBusMenu, and nothing shows without one. An item without a DBusMenu shows its own menu. An item that is only a menu (`ItemIsMenu`, or one refusing `Activate`) opens it on `item.activate()` too. |
| `action close()` | The popup closed: the app is told, and `opened` becomes false. |

### `TrayMenuItem`

An entry of a tray item's menu (DBusMenu), keyed by `id`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `int` | Its id in its menu. |
| `item` | `text` | The tray item whose menu holds it. |
| `label` | `text` | Its label, without mnemonic underscores. |
| `enabled` | `bool` | It can be chosen. |
| `kind` | `text` | `standard` or `separator`. |
| `toggle` | `text` | `none`, `checkmark` or `radio`. |
| `checked` | `bool` | Its check mark or radio button is on. |
| `icon` | `text?` | Its icon: an icon name, or the path of the picture the app sent. |
| `shortcut` | `text?` | Its keyboard shortcut, if it has one (`Control+S`). |
| `children` | `[TrayMenuItem]` | Its submenu's entries; empty when it has none. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action activate()` | Chooses it: the app is told it was clicked. |
| `action open()` | Opens its submenu: the app is told (and may update the entries first). |

### `Window`

A toplevel window, from `ext-foreign-toplevel-list`, with what the
compositor's IPC adds.

Keyed by `id`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `text` | Its identity: the compositor's id when its IPC is used, else the protocol's identifier. |
| `title` | `text` | Its title: `windows.focused?.title`. |
| `app_id` | `text` | The app's id, such as `firefox`. |
| `icon` | `text` | An icon name for its app. |
| `workspace` | `int?` | The workspace it is on, when known. |
| `focused` | `bool` | It has focus. |
| `minimized` | `bool` | It is minimised. |
| `maximized` | `bool` | It is maximised. |
| `fullscreen` | `bool` | It is fullscreen.  `win.fullscreen()` makes it fullscreen, or restores it when it is fullscreen. |
| `urgent` | `bool` | It asks for attention. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action focus()` | Raises and focuses it. |
| `action close()` | Asks it to close. |
| `action minimize()` | Minimises it. |
| `action maximize()` | `win.maximize()` maximises it, or restores it when it is maximised. |
| `action fullscreen()` | It is fullscreen.  `win.fullscreen()` makes it fullscreen, or restores it when it is fullscreen. |

### `Workspace`

A workspace, from `ext-workspace-v1`, keyed by `id`.

| Field | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `int` | Its identity. |
| `name` | `text` | Its name. |
| `focused` | `bool` | It is the focused workspace (at most one is; with the standard protocols alone and several screens, none is). |
| `active` | `bool` | It is shown on its screen (one per screen). |
| `occupied` | `bool` | It holds windows. |
| `urgent` | `bool` | A window on it asks for attention. |
| `screen` | `text` | The name of the screen it is on. |
| `windows` | `[Window]` | Its windows, keyed by `id`. |

| Method | |
| --- | --- |
| `action focus()` | Switches to it: `on click { ws.focus() }`. |

## Opaque types

Values with no structure a program can see, made by functions and read by props.

`Easing`, `Filter`, `HitArea`, `Mask`, `Palette`, `Pose`, `Spring`, `Sprite`, `SwapTransition`, `TokenSet`
